decks.domain: Signs, work zones and school zones

cards.front: Complete the rule: Traffic-sign shape and color both help a driver.
cards.back: Traffic-sign shape and color both help a driver recognize a sign and the action it requires.

cards.front: Complete the rule: In poor visibility such as fog, a driver.
cards.back: In poor visibility such as fog, a driver may be able to recognize only the sign’s shape.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Drivers must recognize and obey.
cards.back: Drivers must recognize and obey traffic signs, signals and roadway markings.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Traffic signs are grouped by function.
cards.back: Traffic signs are grouped by function as regulatory, warning or information-guide signs.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Red traffic-control signs convey stop, yield.
cards.back: Red traffic-control signs convey stop, yield, do not enter or wrong-way instructions.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The stop sign has eight sides and requires.
cards.back: The stop sign has eight sides and requires a full stop before the intersection, with yielding to traffic close enough to be an immediate hazard.

cards.front: Complete the rule: If a stop-controlled intersection has a.
cards.back: If a stop-controlled intersection has a crosswalk, stop before entering that crosswalk.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a yield sign, reduce to a reasonable.
cards.back: At a yield sign, reduce to a reasonable speed and yield to every vehicle on the roadway you are joining.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not enter a roadway marked Do Not.
cards.back: Do not enter a roadway marked Do Not Enter; it may be one-way or closed to all vehicle traffic.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A black arrow or symbol crossed by a.
cards.back: A black arrow or symbol crossed by a red circle and slash prohibits the action pictured.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Regulatory signs give required actions or maximum.
cards.back: Regulatory signs give required actions or maximum travel speeds, and drivers must obey their rules.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The regulatory signs described in this section are.
cards.back: The regulatory signs described in this section are rectangular with black lettering or symbols on white.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Within a Do Not Pass area, do.
cards.back: Within a Do Not Pass area, do not pass a vehicle traveling in your direction.

cards.front: Complete the rule: After passing a Pass With Care sign, passing.
cards.back: After passing a Pass With Care sign, passing other vehicles is permitted again when done carefully.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A No U Turn sign.
cards.back: A No U Turn sign prohibits reversing direction at that intersection.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A No Left Turn sign prohibits.
cards.back: A No Left Turn sign prohibits a left turn at that intersection.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Keep Right sign directs traffic.
cards.back: A Keep Right sign directs traffic to the right side of an obstruction.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A posted speed-limit sign sets the maximum speed.
cards.back: A posted speed-limit sign sets the maximum speed from its location until another speed-limit sign changes it.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Limited nighttime visibility may require.
cards.back: Limited nighttime visibility may require a speed below the posted maximum.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Speed Zone Ahead sign warns.
cards.back: A Speed Zone Ahead sign warns that a reduced speed limit is approaching.

decks.domain: Signs, work zones and school zones

cards.front: Complete the rule: Warning signs use black and yellow.
cards.back: Warning signs use black and yellow and generally have a diamond shape.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The railroad-crossing-ahead warning is round and is the.
cards.back: The railroad-crossing-ahead warning is round and is the only round warning traffic sign described by the handbook.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Crossroad warning indicates a four-way intersection and.
cards.back: A Crossroad warning indicates a four-way intersection and calls for watching traffic entering across the road.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Winding Road sign warns of.
cards.back: A Winding Road sign warns of a sequence of turns or curves ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a T-intersection warning, the road ahead does.
cards.back: At a T-intersection warning, the road ahead does not continue straight and turns right and left.

cards.front: Complete the rule: An angled Side Road sign warns of a.
cards.back: An angled Side Road sign warns of a side road joining the highway at an angle.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The right-side Side Road sign warns.
cards.back: The right-side Side Road sign warns of a roadway joining from the right.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Sharp Right Turn warning.
cards.back: A Sharp Right Turn warning identifies a sharp right turn ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Sharp Left and Right Turn warning identifies.
cards.back: A Sharp Left and Right Turn warning identifies a sharp left turn followed by a sharp right turn.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Right and Left Curves warning identifies.
cards.back: A Right and Left Curves warning identifies a right curve followed by a left curve.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Railroad Crossing warning.
cards.back: A Railroad Crossing warning indicates a rail crossing ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a School Ahead warning, slow down.
cards.back: At a School Ahead warning, slow down and watch for children at any time.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Loose Gravel warning indicates.
cards.back: A Loose Gravel warning indicates loose gravel on the highway ahead.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A One Lane Bridge warning means there is.
cards.back: A One Lane Bridge warning means there is no room to meet or pass another car or truck on the bridge.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Range Cattle warning indicates that cattle.
cards.back: A Range Cattle warning indicates that cattle or horses may be on an unfenced highway.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Road Narrows warning indicates a narrower road.
cards.back: A Road Narrows warning indicates a narrower road ahead that still leaves room to meet and pass.

cards.front: Complete the rule: An Icy Road sign warns that.
cards.back: An Icy Road sign warns that the road is icy and dangerous.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a School Bus Stop Ahead warning.
cards.back: At a School Bus Stop Ahead warning, begin reducing speed for the approaching bus stop.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Stop Ahead warning calls for beginning.
cards.back: A Stop Ahead warning calls for beginning to slow for the approaching stop sign.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A right-curve warning may carry a.
cards.back: A right-curve warning may carry a suggested safe curve speed below it.

decks.domain: Signs, work zones and school zones

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a School Crossing Ahead warning.
cards.back: At a School Crossing Ahead warning, slow down and keep watching for children.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The School Crossing sign identifies where children cross.
cards.back: The School Crossing sign identifies where children cross and requires stopping when pedestrians are waiting to cross.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a Pedestrian Crossing warning, reduce speed, watch.
cards.back: At a Pedestrian Crossing warning, reduce speed, watch for people in your path and be ready to stop.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a Low Clearance warning, do not proceed.
cards.back: At a Low Clearance warning, do not proceed if the vehicle is too tall to pass beneath the overpass.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Hill warning signals a steep grade where.
cards.back: A Hill warning signals a steep grade where the driver should check the brakes and may need a lower gear.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Divided Highway Begins sign warns of a.
cards.back: A Divided Highway Begins sign warns of a median separating two one-way roadways and directs drivers to keep right.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Divided Highway Ends warning means the road.
cards.back: A Divided Highway Ends warning means the road becomes a single roadway carrying traffic both ways, where drivers should keep right.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a Deer Crossing warning, stay alert.
cards.back: At a Deer Crossing warning, stay alert and reduce speed if a deer appears.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A Cattle Crossing warning marks a place.
cards.back: A Cattle Crossing warning marks a place where livestock is driven between farm areas.

cards.front: Complete the rule: At a Slippery When Wet warning, reduce speed.
cards.back: At a Slippery When Wet warning, reduce speed, avoid hard braking or abrupt turns and leave more following space.

decks.domain: Signs, work zones and school zones

cards.front: Complete the rule: Orange is the basic color used.
cards.back: Orange is the basic color used for construction and maintenance traffic-control devices.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Work-area warning signs are mostly.
cards.back: Work-area warning signs are mostly diamond-shaped, although some are rectangular.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Construction and maintenance signs warn of unusual or.
cards.back: Construction and maintenance signs warn of unusual or potentially dangerous conditions near work areas and call for a cautious approach.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Exceeding the posted speed in a.
cards.back: Exceeding the posted speed in a construction or work zone is a violation.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The diagonal stripes on barricades or vertical panels.
cards.back: The diagonal stripes on barricades or vertical panels show the side on which traffic should pass.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Stripes descending toward the right.
cards.back: Stripes descending toward the right direct traffic to bear right.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Stripes descending toward the left.
cards.back: Stripes descending toward the left direct traffic to bear left.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Barricades, panels, drums, cones and tubes warn of.
cards.back: Barricades, panels, drums, cones and tubes warn of work-area hazards and guide traffic, often using steady or flashing lights at night.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Work-zone arrow panels can operate by day or.
cards.back: Work-zone arrow panels can operate by day or night to guide vehicles into lanes and warn that part of the road ahead is closed.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Work-zone flaggers may stop, slow.
cards.back: Work-zone flaggers may stop, slow or guide traffic through the area.

cards.front: Complete the rule: The handbook describes flaggers wearing orange clothing and.
cards.back: The handbook describes flaggers wearing orange clothing and directing traffic with red flags or stop-and-slow paddles.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Traffic fines are.
cards.back: Traffic fines are doubled in work zones.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Construction and work zones have no single standard.
cards.back: Construction and work zones have no single standard speed limit; the transportation department, local authority, utility company or private contractor sets a limit for each zone.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Knowingly or negligently driving through a highway construction.
cards.back: Knowingly or negligently driving through a highway construction zone in a way that endangers people or property can lead to a Reckless Endangerment of a Highway Worker charge.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Removing, ignoring or intentionally striking a traffic-control device.
cards.back: Removing, ignoring or intentionally striking a traffic-control device in the stated highway construction-zone circumstances may also lead to a Reckless Endangerment of a Highway Worker charge.

decks.domain: Signs, work zones and school zones

cards.front: Complete the rule: Check speed and slow near schools at any.
cards.back: Check speed and slow near schools at any hour, watching for children near schools and parks during both day and night.

cards.front: Complete the rule: School-zone limits may be as.
cards.back: School-zone limits may be as low as fifteen miles per hour.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Drivers must stop and remain stopped.
cards.back: Drivers must stop and remain stopped for pedestrians in crosswalks and at intersections.

cards.front: Complete the rule: A school zone includes the campus, adjoining streets.
cards.back: A school zone includes the campus, adjoining streets and additional surrounding blocks designated by the local authority setting a special limit.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Always yield to pedestrians in a school crosswalk.
cards.back: Always yield to pedestrians in a school crosswalk, whether or not a crossing guard is present.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Stop before a school crosswalk so.
cards.back: Stop before a school crosswalk so other drivers can see the pedestrians.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not drive through a.
cards.back: Do not drive through a column of schoolchildren crossing a roadway.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Do not pass a school crossing guard who.
cards.back: Do not pass a school crossing guard who is directing children across the road while holding the official sign in its stop position.

cards.front: Complete the rule: School-zone signs, road markings and flashing lights.
cards.back: School-zone signs, road markings and flashing lights can indicate an authorized change in speed limit.

cards.front: Complete the rule: School-zone parking and stopping signs can keep.
cards.back: School-zone parking and stopping signs can keep travel lanes, sightlines and bus loading zones clear.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Speeding fines are doubled.
cards.back: Speeding fines are doubled in Montana school zones.

cards.front: Complete the rule: Children approaching school may cross without understanding traffic.
cards.back: Children approaching school may cross without understanding traffic controls or accurately judging a vehicle’s speed and distance.

cards.front: Complete the rule: School pickup and drop-off congestion can add.
cards.back: School pickup and drop-off congestion can add confusion to parking lots and nearby streets.
